summary: Source-anchored research for analyzeShardKey and query sampling. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Operators can inspect query-sampling progress with $currentOp and inspect captured queries with $listSampledQueries. Inspecting captured command types helps check what the workload sample contains. (medium confidence)

Representative query sampling can require several days. The mongosh example evaluates keys using seven days of sampled workload, so a short or quiet interval should not be assumed to characterize a full application cycle. (medium confidence)

SERVER-119912 reports that key-characteristic passes scan the supporting index even when sampleSize is small. SERVER-107799 independently explains the deliberate index-scan approach for these metrics. A small sampleSize therefore should not be treated as a guarantee of proportionally small scan cost; confirm behavior on the deployed build. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29)

Atlas Shard Key Advisor documentation specifies five query samples per second, seven-day sample retention, and manual disabling when sampling is no longer needed. Its UI sampling rate cannot be adjusted through Shard Key Advisor. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

SERVER-119912 reports index scans proportional to collection size despite a smaller sampleSize for key-characteristic analysis. Treat this as an implementation warning, not proof about every release; the issue names no affected versions or shipped fix. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-29)

analyzeShardKey accepts a candidate key for an unsharded or sharded collection, or the current key of a sharded collection. It reports metrics rather than performing the sharding change. (medium confidence)

MongoDB introduced analyzeShardKey and configureQueryAnalyzer in 7.0 to support shard-key evaluation; Percona also included these commands in its 7.0 release line, and ApsaraDB documents the analysis workflow for its users. (medium confidence)

Document sampling and query sampling are distinct: sampleRate or sampleSize controls the documents used for key characteristics, while configureQueryAnalyzer collects operations for read/write distribution. Key-characteristic analysis can run without query sampling. (high confidence)

Key-characteristic metrics include cardinality, frequency and monotonicity. Read/write distribution metrics describe routing patterns and the hotness of candidate-key ranges; they require sampled application queries. (medium confidence)

analyzeShardKey does not block collection reads or writes. MongoDB and Alibaba recommend secondary or secondaryPreferred read preference to reduce production impact; non-blocking operation does not establish negligible resource consumption. (high confidence)

SERVER-107799 records that random document sampling for range boundaries did not always yield the expected representative sample and could interfere with read/write distribution output. This issue concerns boundary construction, distinct from collecting application-query samples. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-11)

Historical engineering work motivating document sampling reported analysis taking hours on collections with hundreds of millions of documents and high-cardinality keys. This is historical evidence of analysis overhead, not a latency forecast for current deployments. (low confidence)
MongoDB introduced analyzeShardKey in 7.0 for evaluating existing or prospective shard keys; its output separates key characteristics from read/write distribution. (high confidence)
Routing metrics require sampled operations. A zero or absent distribution result without samples is not evidence that production queries have zero routing cost. (low confidence)

configureQueryAnalyzer enables collection sampling with mode full and samplesPerSecond, and disables it with mode off. Operators can inspect captured operations with $listSampledQueries and monitor sampling through $currentOp. (low confidence)

Sampling consumes storage: MongoDB keeps sampled queries in an internal TTL-indexed collection and expires them according to queryAnalysisSampleExpirationSecs. Disable sampling after collecting sufficient evidence. (low confidence)

MongoDB ties routing-metric quality to workload representativeness and warns that some applications need several days of query sampling; there is no universal adequate collection window. (low confidence)
